content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, tracing each limitation, part, and depicted relationship back to the disclosure text.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed. I traced all 16 claims (1-10 apparatus, 11-16 method) limitation by limitation, all 25 numerals in draft/numerals.md (100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 140, 202-216), every numbered part and relationship in the Summary, Detailed Description, Abstract and Brief Description of Drawings, and every structure, connection and leader statement in figures/FIG-1.md through FIG-4.md, against the affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md and input/conversation.md. Supported and traced without issue: the branch whose limit is lower than the sum of connector ratings; the per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; the branch current sensor upstream of the connector contactors measuring total branch current as an independent safety input; the isolated local bus to the interfaces and contactors; the stored charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value; the allocation interval subtracting measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve; minimum-sustaining-first assignment then deficit-based distribution; pilot delivery of assigned limits and per-connector verification; reduced pilot command, verification interval and one-at-a-time ordered shedding in a stored order until branch current is below the limit (including claim 2's re-measurement after each opening, which the "until measured branch current is below" condition entails); the three reclosure conditions including randomized recovery delay; welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold, inhibition of the other contactors on the branch, and the local fault indicator; network interface, signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage behaviour, token expiry gating of new sessions, tamper-evident meter sequence and upload on return; and the service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time with storage only on sensor agreement. Numeral integrity checked: each numeral maps to exactly one part, each appears in the description and in at least one figure brief, and FIG. 4's stated count of seven rectangles plus one diamond matches the eight numbered steps 202-216 and the description's flow, including the diamond return at step 210 and the reclosure return at step 216. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions or unresolved alternatives remain, and there are no section-line designations to reconcile. Three defects found. Critically, the description and the FIG. 2 brief route the connector current sensor's signal over the isolated local bus ("coupled to the connector current sensor 124 ... over the isolated local bus 108"; bus "carries ... the measured connector currents"; a dashed sensing line that "meets the isolated local bus line inside the dashed rectangle"), but the only affirmative source statement about the bus is "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus," which enumerates the sensor separately from the control-pilot interface and never places it on the bus; this is an untraced connection topology assertion, and notably claim 5 correctly recites the bus as coupling only to the control-pilot interfaces and contactors, so the description also conflicts with the claim it supports. A minor formalities defect ("thelarge") appears in the FIG. 3 brief. Note on scope: prior_art/ files were not part of this material, so the Background's prior-art characterizations were not traced here and are left to the later citation review; the brief also states no prior-art search was run, so the art relied on may be incomplete. I did not inspect rendered images, and I assessed only source fidelity and internal consistency, not patentability.

findings.title: Description routes the connector current sensor signal over the isolated local bus, which the disclosure never states
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 1 paragraph ("An edge controller 106 ... isolated local bus 108") and FIG. 2 paragraph
findings.detail: Two sentences assert that the isolated local bus carries the connector-current measurements and that the controller is coupled to the connector current sensor over that bus. The disclosure describes the bus only as the path to the connector interfaces and the contactors, and it lists the connector current sensor as a separate per-connector element from the control-pilot interface. No affirmative USER passage places the connector current sensors on the isolated local bus or otherwise specifies how their measurements reach the controller. This is an untraced connection/topology assertion, and it also conflicts with claim 5, which recites the bus as coupling the controller only "to the control-pilot interfaces ... and to the contactors". Coupling of the controller to the sensors as such is supported ("verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor"); only the routing over the bus is unsupported.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The isolated local bus 108 carries, between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, the assigned current limits, the contactor commands, the pilot reports and the measured connector currents." and "The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md, para. 1), showing the gap: "Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier. ... A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." There is no source passage stating that the connector current sensor communicates over the isolated local bus.
findings.fix: In the FIG. 1 paragraph, replace "the assigned current limits, the contactor commands, the pilot reports and the measured connector currents." with "the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports." In the FIG. 2 paragraph, replace "The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124." with "The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124."

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief depicts the connector current sensor's sensing line joining the isolated local bus
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md, paragraph beginning "A dashed line leaves the square outline representing the connector current sensor"
findings.detail: The brief instructs that the sensing connection from the connector current sensor terminates on the isolated local bus line inside the connector channel. That is a substantive connection and flow-path assertion (the sensor's measurement travels on the bus), not a depiction convention, and it has no affirmative inventor support. The disclosure places only the connector interfaces and contactors on the bus. Depicting a sensing connection from the sensor toward the controller is supported, but it must not be shown as joining the bus.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A dashed line leaves the square outline representing the connector current sensor, runs left below the horizontal run and clear of the control-pilot interface block, and meets the isolated local bus line inside the dashed rectangle, as the sensing connection by which the edge controller receives the measured connector current." Nearest source (input/disclosure.md, para. 1): "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." No source passage connects the connector current sensor to the bus.
findings.fix: Replace that paragraph with: "A dashed line leaves the square outline representing the connector current sensor, runs left below the horizontal run and clear of the control-pilot interface block, and crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle above the isolated local bus line and clear of it, as the sensing connection by which the edge controller receives the measured connector current. It touches no other line and crosses no other line and no leader."

findings.title: Missing word space in the FIG. 3 brief
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, paragraph beginning "A further empty rectangle stands outside the large rectangle"
findings.detail: A typographical run-together of two words appears in the figure brief text; it should be corrected before render and filing so the brief reads cleanly.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A solid line crosses the right side of thelarge rectangle and meets the left side of the local fault indicator rectangle."
findings.fix: Replace "the right side of thelarge rectangle" with "the right side of the large rectangle".
